turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Hi Dana, Leo from HyperSale. Quick question: how long does it take your new reps to sound confident on live buyer calls?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: We already have Gong for this. What exactly are you calling about?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Totally—Gong shows what happened after the call; HyperSale lets reps practise realistic buyer conversations beforehand. Are managers coaching from recordings today?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Not consistently—managers usually listen only after a deal is lost, so new hires end up practicing on live prospects. But my managers don’t have time for another tool.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: That’s where we fit: reps practise independently, and managers review scored moments with exact quotes instead of full calls. Would a 30-day pilot help?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Maybe, but how would I even measure whether the practice works—ramp time, attach rate, pipeline coverage, or something else?

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: I’d start with ramp time and one Gong behavior, like objection handling, then compare pilot reps with the prior cohort. Which matters most?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: Ramp time is the priority; new hires are learning objection handling on live prospects. But we just renewed Gong, so there’s no budget this year.

turns.speaker: rep
turns.text: Understood—we wouldn’t replace Gong. Could we scope a 30-day new-hire pilot and use ramp-time improvement to build next year’s business case?

turns.speaker: buyer
turns.text: If you can keep the pilot under $15k, I can sponsor a 20-minute scoping call with our enablement lead next week—send an invite and proposed ramp-time success criteria. I’ve got a meeting, I need to go.
